unverifiable_exemptions: Units not intended to be used as a person's primary residence
coverage.summary: Applies in Jersey City to any real estate lessor, meaning any individual or entity that owns real property and leases it as a residential dwelling unit. There is no limit on building size, unit count or construction date. A residential dwelling unit is any house, apartment, accessory unit or other unit intended as a person's primary residence. Inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities are excluded.

result.notes: I removed other_conditions (licensed real estate agents excluded) because it limits who counts as a service provider, not which buildings, units or owners are covered. I removed owner_conditions (owners of multiple properties) because that exemption carves out conduct from the 'coordinating' definition: actions related exclusively to properties the same owner controls. It does not exclude any owner class or building. That conduct is landlord conduct and belongs in exemptions or requirement, not coverage. requires_unknown_facts is set to false because the rule reaches all ordinary residential rentals: any house, apartment or accessory unit leased by any owning entity. The primary-residence intent qualifier cannot be checked from assessor data, so it is listed in unverifiable_exemptions. No unit-count threshold appears in § 218-12 despite its placement in Chapter 218 (Multiple Dwellings), so min_units stays null. The FAIR Act preemption concern in conflict_note is not supported by any provided document, so the preemption fields remain null.
